item.title: Tenth Circuit rules in favor of NCAA in Wisne eligibility lawsuit, overturns injunction
item.description: In a landmark legal win for the NCAA, the Tenth Circuit ruled in the governing body’s favor in the Wisne eligibility lawsuit on Friday. As a result, the injunction has been overturned as athletes sought a fifth year. The suit was filed in Colorado over the summer in light of the NCAA’s age-based, five-year eligibility model. Upon implementation, the new rule was not retroactive to members of the class of 2022, and a number of legal challenges followed. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Judge Charlotte Sweeney of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Colorado ruled in favor of the class by granting a nationwide injunction. In September, though, the Tenth Circuit granted the NCAA’s request for a stay of the injunction, which meant it was on pause pending a ruling from the court. Attorneys for both the plaintiffs and the NCAA argued before the three-judge panel Oct. 13. During oral arguments, the judges said one of the central parts of the case was figuring out how the athletes would be harmed if they were not declared eligible. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter “It doesn’t seem there’s been a definition of the market from a huge, huge division – golf, everything,” U.S. Circuit Judge Paul Kelly said during the hearing, via the AP . “And you’re lumping them all together and you never looked at commonality and interchangeability of the various buyers.” While the court stayed the Wisne injunction, more lawsuits were filed at the state level. The NCAA won out in some of those cases, including in Kentucky, Arizona and Ohio. As a result, athletes in those cases would not be eligible pending a final ruling. The Kentucky case notably includes Thomas Castellanos , who played four games for the Red Raiders after securing a preliminary injunction. However, after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dissolved the temporary injunction, his availability came into question while awaiting a hearing. A judge then granted a motion for a new injunction , and Castellanos suited up for Texas Tech vs. Arizona State . The NCAA announced implementation of its five-year, age-based eligibility model this summer. Athletes will now get five years to play five seasons, with their eligibility “clock” starting at their 19th birthday or the date they enroll at a university, whichever happens first. The Tenth Circuit’s ruling also comes as the Protect College Sports Act heads to the U.S. House of Representatives. It advanced out of the Senate by a 77-22 margin in late September and addresses eligibility, among many other issues. The House is not due back in session until after the midterm elections.

item.title: Dianna Russini Set to Return to Media: What We Know
item.description: Dianna Russini is poised to make a sports media comeback soon, Front Office Sports has confirmed, several months after resigning from The Athletic in the aftermath of Page Six publishing photos showing her with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at an adults-only Arizona resort in April. After ProFootballTalk first reported that Russini has told people around the NFL that she is expecting to return to the industry next week, several options have emerged for what comes next. Russini is expected to launch new content sponsored by gambling operators, sources said, adding that there have been talks with Jake Paul’s Betr platform as well as offshore sportsbook BetUS. One source said that Russini has also had talks with iHeart. FOS discovered a new X/Twitter page titled “Russini Report,” created in October, that only has three followers—Andres Vargas, a content creator and spokesperson for BetUS, and Crossing Lines, a show sponsored by BetUS featuring ex-Barstool personality Jeff Nadu and co-host Donnie Seymour. An additional video manager, named Natalie, also follows the page from a protected account. The “Russini Report” page indicates a show will air live on Wednesdays encompassing pro football news, injuries, and analysis. The page previously indicated the show would be “powered by BetUS,” but that language has since been edited out. Screen grab Basketball Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman is also an endorser of BetUS, which is headquartered in Costa Rica. On Wednesday, Page Six reported that Russini will be “headlining her own show” on a digital platform. “It’s been in the works for a while and she can’t wait to get back to what she loves,” a source told Page Six . Russini stopped responding to messages when presented with BetUS, Betr, and iHeart as places she has had talks with. Her agent, Matt Olson of CAA, referred FOS to the publicist Melissa Nathan, who declined to comment. Spokespeople for BetUS, Betr, and iHeart did not respond to requests for comment, nor did Vargas. Jon “Stugotz” Weiner, a host for iHeart and its subsidiary Fox Sports Radio, has previously said he would welcome the chance to collaborate with Russini again. Russini was a frequent guest on Weiner’s previous show, The Dan Le Batard Show With Stugotz , and also joined Weiner on his I Love Football show during Super Bowl week this past February. If Russini reaches a deal with iHeart, it is not expected to encompass Fox Sports Radio, one source said. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy also previously said he would consider hiring Russini, but he told FOS this week that she is not going to work for Barstool now. Sources told FOS that Kalshi, Underdog, and FanDuel are not in the running to sponsor her content at this time. item.description: Canada is consistently one of the top two nations in the world in women’s lacrosse, and has been for decades. This country has produced some of the greatest lacrosse players in history, like the legendary Dana Dobbie. We are bound to see more greatness from this squad that has a No. 1 ranking in mind to chase after. The roster Canada has put together for the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games is an exciting mixture of seasoned leaders and exploding stars. Let’s break it down. Field Players Erica Evans Annabel Child Jordan Dean Milana Zizakovic Kassidy Morris Aurora Cordingley Maggie Cuddy Nicole Perroni Megan Kinna Madalyn Baxter Kylea Dobson Goalies Kameron Halsall Alecia Nicholas One word to describe this roster is… Poised. This Canadian team is primed and prepped for a big tournament. They have battled to the very end against USA the last few times the rival nations have matched up in a Sixes Championship, and are likely itching to get over that hump. Players like Erica Evans , Megan Kinna, Nicole Perroni and Aurora Cordingley have played on these big stages in a Canadian uniform before. Evans brings a decade of familiarity alone, playing with the Canadian national team since 2015. Their experience from playing for Canada for many years will bring a level of poise and comfort to the Global Lacrosse Games that’s needed to thrive and win against the other top nations in the world. Biggest star: Erica Evans Evans is coming off a championship summer with the Maryland Charm and has been an international star since she won a gold medal with the U19 Canadian team. Evans will be the main all-around Canadian player to keep an eye on throughout each game. item.description: Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool in the summer from Paris Saint-Germain -Credit:Carl Recine, Getty Images Glen Johnson has addressed comments from France FIFA World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit, suggesting Liverpool overpaid for 'overrated' £123 million ($166.6 million) summer acquisition Bradley Barcola. The former Reds defender has expressed confidence that the winger will find his form following a challenging beginning to his Anfield tenure. Barcola toiled in an unaccustomed striker's position on Wednesday as Liverpool's flawless UEFA Champions League league phase record ended with a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahçe in Istanbul. The France international had shone in his prior Champions League road fixture, delivering an impressive hat-trick during the 6-3 winat LASK. -Credit:Laurence Griffiths, Getty Images However, those strikes represent the sole goals Barcola has managed across his 13 outings for the Reds following his blockbuster transfer from European champions Paris Saint-Germain on August 31. Earlier this month, former Arsenal, Barcelona, and Chelsea midfielder Petit, who captured the World Cup with France in 1998, stated via the Liverpool Echo : "£120m? I would never put that price tag on the table. We all know that in France. "We know that he is a quality player, he could sometimes be great, but he doesn't have consistency during games. He was good most of the time with Paris because of the whole team behind him. I would probably have spent £60m or £70m, maximum. That's my opinion. It's becoming common now that English clubs are spending so much money on overrated players." However, Johnson, who registered 200 appearances for Liverpool with nine goals and 13 assists following his £17.5 million (around $29 million) transfer from Portsmouth in June 2009, considers Barcola "world-class" and argues he shouldn't be evaluated solely on his price tag. He said: "I don't think Barcola is overrated. I think he's world-class. I've been a fan of his for a long time. I think he's brilliant. item.description: VfB Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen preview: Undav and Füllkrug in contrasting form ahead of Topspiel Deniz Undav's VfB Stuttgart will host Niclas Füllkrug's Werder Bremen in the marquee fixture of matchday 10. VfB Stuttgart The captain's goal drought contributed to Stuttgart's slow start to the season. Undav had found the net twice, but none of those goals came in the league as his poor form led him to miss out on Jürgen Klopp's squad nomination for the second time. Meanwhile, Ermedin Demirović has been their go-to guy this season, although he was unable to score in the defeat against Galatasaray, who had an unsuccessful attempt to sign the Bosnian striker in the summer. Team News The absence of Atakan Karazor and Angelo Stiller in midfield would cause selection issues for Hoeneß, although the former has a slight chance to recover from an injury that forced his early substitution against Galatasaray. Demirović and Undav started together against both Leverkusen and the Turkish champions, although Hoeneß preferred different playing systems. In goal, Dennis Seimen is expected to return in place of the experienced Fabian Bredlow. Werder Bremen After matching Rudi Völler's club record of scoring in seven successive Bundesliga games, Füllkrug earned a national team call-up by Klopp on Thursday. The 33-year-old leads the scoring chart in Bundesliga, and he already opened a five-goal lead over a certain Harry Kane. The nine goals from the former Torjägerkanone winner helped Werder Bremen to start the matchday in fifth place after having to fight relegation consistently in past seasons. Daniel Thioune’s troops are unbeaten in Bundesliga since starting the campaign with a 4-1 defeat to Freiburg. Eren Dinkci, who scored the second goal after replacing him, is expected to start in the right wing. Head-to-head Werder Bremen are unbeaten in their last two trips to Stuttgart, although the Swabians did win 4-0 at Weserstadion last season. item.title: Orlando City legend Robin Jansson announces retirement
item.description: Orlando City legend Robin Jansson announces retirement By Jaime Uribarri TRANSFER TRACKER STATUS: Retirement Orlando City defender Robin Jansson has announced his retirement from professional soccer after the 2026 MLS season, ending a legendary eight-year career with the Lions. The 34-year-old center back joined Orlando in March 2019 from from AIK Fotboll in his native Sweden. He helped the club lift the first trophy of their MLS era, the 2022 US Open Cup , and reach the 2024 Eastern Conference Final. Jansson was named captain ahead of the 2024 season amid a historic run that saw him set club records for appearances (263), starts (256) and minutes played (23,050) across all competitions. He's the longest-tenured player in Orlando City history. "First, I want to say it's been a pleasure to wear this jersey and fight for this crest. When I signed here eight seasons ago, I didn't know I would be here for that long,” said Jansson. “Together, we set new standards and brought home the club's first trophy of the MLS era. I was proud and honored to be given the captain's armband along the way. I've really enjoyed it and have been doing what I love for so many years at the same club. I have been treated very well during my time here, and it has become a place I can call home and will always be connected to. "But now it's time to step aside and retire from the game I grew up loving and dreaming about." Jansson helped guide Orlando to their debut Audi MLS Cup Playoffs appearance in 2020, the first of seven straight postseason berths for the league's longest active streak. He was also a key member of the Lions side that reached the MLS is Back Tournament Final in 2020 and qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup for the first time in 2023. The club will recognize and celebrate Jansson following Saturday's Decision Day regular-season finale vs. the New England Revolution at Inter.co Stadium (4 pm ET | Apple TV ). “Robin will always hold a special place in the history of this club, and for me personally, because he was the first player I signed for Orlando City,” said sporting director and general manager Ricardo Moreira. “From the moment he arrived, he embraced everything this club stands for and grew into one of the most important figures in our history. He is a club legend, not only because of his performances and accomplishments, but because of the person, leader and teammate he has been throughout his time here. "We love Robin and his family, and we wish them nothing but happiness and success in this next chapter of his life.” READ MORE: MLS Transfer Tracker

item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Laken Tomlinson #72 and Jordan Morgan #77 of the Green Bay Packers in action against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates a touchdown against the Detroit Lions during the third quarter at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers surprisingly started offensive lineman Laken Tomlinson at right guard in Week 8 despite having one start on that side of the offensive line in his 12-year NFL career. Tomlinson noted that the transition is going great, but it was a lot tougher last week given the short week and lack of practice time. “I mean, it’s definitely a challenge, especially last week,” admitted Tomlinson. Tomlinson started for the Packers at left guard in Week 7. So, he practiced on the left side leading up to the game. Green Bay Packers Guard Laken Tomlinson Opens Up on Changing Sides Getty Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers Because the Packers played on Thursday night in Week 8, the team did not have a legitimate practice. So, Tomlinson had to change sides without much work in team drills. Tomlinson noted that the flip side is that this week gives him extra time to prepare for staying on the right side. “This week, especially going into the long weekend, I had some extra time to kind of just like go over some stuff on my own,” said Tomlinson. “Work on my technique and just work on flipping things technique-wise, and having these two days of practice. So definitely a lot more comfortable now.” Tomlinson has 11,131 snaps at left guard in his NFL career. After his Week 8 start, he has 131 snaps at right guard. The Packers coaching staff noted that Tomlinson was playing so well that they could not bench him. However, with starter Aaron Banks back in the lineup, the team could not keep him on the left side. item.description: TIME MACHINE: GENOA vs. AC MILAN Before the international break, it was an away match against Genoa. After the home Derby, the Rossoneri were back on the road for Matchday 11 of Serie A, heading to the Stadio L. Ferraris in Genoa's Marassi district, where on December 2, 2011 , AC Milan produced a convincing 2-0 win, inspired by the brilliance of Zlatan Ibrahimović and a strong all-around team performance. This was Allegri’s second season in charge, with the reigning champions still in excellent form. It was a wintery Friday night, and Van Bommel, Pato and Abbiati were all unavailable. It was not quite an injury crisis, but hardly ideal preparation for an important, tricky fixture. The Rossoneri were coming off a dominant 4-0 win over ChievoVerona at San Siro and had not lost since the start of October, when they were lost away against Juventus, their closest rivals in the title race. It was not a straightforward evening, with play briefly interrupted by crowd trouble inside the stadium. Ibrahimović and Nocerino proved to be a dangerous combination. Early on, the striker twice picked out the midfielder's runs, with Nocerino denied first by Rossi and then by Frey from close range. Robinho, Boateng and Nocerino all had further attempts without finding the target, before Ibra forced another save from Frey. Genoa grew into the game late in the first half: Amelia punched away a dangerous Veloso free kick, while Mesto failed to capitalize on a mix-up between Thiago Silva and Yepes in possession. The turning point came in the 56th minute . Robinho sent Ibrahimović through, and the Swede was brought down inside the box by former AC Milan defender Kaladze , who was shown a second yellow card and sent off. Penalty: Ibrahimović made no mistake, drilling his spot kick home to give AC Milan the lead. The closing stages were more comfortable, although Robinho somehow missed from point-blank range and Rossi went close with a backheel that drifted wide. Then, in the 79th minute , AC Milan put the result beyond doubt. Boateng delivered into the box and Nocerino arrived to finish calmly from close range. 2-0 to the Rossoneri , who would ultimately fall short in their bid to retain the title at the end of the 2011/12 season. item.title: Forget the schedule, Jalen Brunson has another theory to explain the NBA injury crisis
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Almost every team in the NBA has been hit by injuries this season. We are less than a month into the new campaign, and several big names have already been sidelined due to one issue or another. There are fears that the list could grow in the coming weeks and months. Many feel the schedule is the reason why, but Jalen Brunson has a different theory. Jalen Brunson says the NBA’s injury crisis could be down to ‘style of play’ It has been a real shame to see several fantastic players miss games due to injuries this season. From Anthony Edwards and Ja Morant to Paolo Banchero and Kawhi Leonard, many are currently sidelined, causing their respective teams to be significantly weaker. Several theories have been going around – from the gruelling schedule to a lack of preparation in pre-season practice sessions. But Jalen Brunson thinks it may actually be down to the style of play most coaches employ in the NBA in today’s game. When told that 16-20 per cent of the league is on the injury report, Brunson said on the Roommates Show : “I just feel like it’s a lot. “Is the schedule asking too much of the players? No! I mean, the schedule is the schedule. It’s been that way for – we’ve been playing 82 games for, I don’t know how many years – like decades. “But it’s obviously unfortunate things happen, but yeah, I don’t think it’s the scheduling part. I think maybe it’s like the style of play. We’re playing fast-paced basketball.” The intensity involved in almost every team sport in the world has gone up in recent years, and it is showing no signs of slowing down. That has definitely made games more interesting, but it has to be said that the physical burden on players has gone up as well. That increases the risk of injuries, which we are all seeing right now. item.title: Worcestershire trio aim to make more Cup magic
item.description: It's now 55 seasons since non-league Hereford United's 2-1 fourth-round replay win over top-flight Newcastle United entered English football folklore as arguably the greatest FA Cup shock of all time. Elsewhere in the Midlands, though, there have been many other upsets and moments of cup magic too. Telford United (in 1984) and Kidderminster Harriers (in 1994) both made it to the fifth round, and Worcestershire village side Alvechurch hold a record they will keep forever - unless the rules are changed again - after taking four replays to see off Oxford City in a qualifying round tie in 1971. Worcester City were involved in a record-breaking penalty shootout against Scunthorpe in 2014 - the same year they famously beat Coventry City. But, while the memory of that day at Hereford - Ronnie Radford et al - surpasses all other memories, across the Worcestershire border, it perhaps still irks a bit. Accompanied by fallen 1970s non-league stars Stafford Rangers, Worcestershire clubs make up three of the four non-EFL Midlands sides to have made it through to the first round proper - the Harriers plus seventh-tier duo Alvechurch and Worcester, who all face EFL clubs. How will they fare this time? Plymouth Argyle v Alvechurch 5th in League One v 6th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier 7) On paper, it looks a very tall order for Alvechurch. But not every non-league club has got an FA Cup pedigree like the Church's manager Kyle Storer. The former Bedworth United, Tamworth, Hinckley United, Atherstone Town, Nuneaton Town, Kiddy Harriers, Wrexham, Cheltenham Town, Solihull Moors, Nuneaton Borough, AFC Telford United, Kettering Town and Alvechurch player is not just a walking advert for Midlands non-league football, he has got plenty of FA Cup "previous" to be taken into consideration. "I've been very fortunate," Storer told BBC Midlands Today. "I got to the fourth round with Kiddy Harriers, when we played at Sunderland in front of 40,000. And that was having beaten Peterborough over two games with a team that had Joe Lolley, Marvin Johnson and Chey Dunkley." Kyle Storer (background) led Kiddy Harriers out for their 1-0 fourth-round defeat by Sunderland at the Stadium of Light [Shutterstock] "And, when I was at Tamworth, we won at Bournemouth [ Storer actually scored the winner] , then took Stoke to a replay. And we got Norwich at home in third round the following year." Dion Dublin and Darren Huckerby both netted twice in a 4-1 win but Storer had the last word by getting one back. "It was voted goal of the round too," he grins. "I've had some amazing FA Cup runs but let's hope we can go and create another day to remember. Let's hope we can cause some damage. "in terms of football prospects, it's a tough one. They're flying, aren't they? But, in financial terms, then it's amazing."
